title: Quantized kernel fallback caused intermittent crash loops and subtle output drift — mitigation & follow-up
creator: Samir Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity reshuffle on 2026-02-18 we rolled kernel-selector heuristics that caused a subset of quantized models (int8 dynamic + per-channel affinities) to hit an unsupported op path. In the majority of cases the serving runtime performed an automatic fallback to a slower dequantized kernel; in ~7% of requests (particular model/sequence-length combos) that fallback triggered a crash-loop and in ~12% of higher-fidelity evaluation prompts we observed measurable semantic drift in outputs compared to the baseline (ROUGE/BLEU style checks + internal evals). This ticket captures the incident follow-ups, short-term mitigations, and tracked action items for a permanent fix.
incident_summary: Timeline: 2026-02-18 03:15 UTC capacity reshuffle and kernel-selector rollout -> 03:44 first spike in 5xx errors -> 04:10 automated rollback to previous selector -> 04:35 crash-loop signals persist for specific quantized model variants -> 06:00 mitigations: pinning model variants + rate-limiting heavy KV cache population -> 2026-02-19 detection of output drift in nightly evals for evaluation prompt set EVAL-quant-medium. Impact: ~0.9% of total hosted requests experienced increased latency, ~0.02% experienced transient 5xx; three customers reported degraded response quality (support tickets #SUP-793, #SUP-794, #SUP-801).
root_cause: The kernel-selector change included an aggressive compatibility assumption: if a custom fused attention op appeared incompatible, the selector scheduled a generic fallback path without fully validating the dequantization ordering and scale broadcasting semantics. This produced two problems: (1) an intermittent memory corruption race in the fallback leading to crash loops for long-running KV cache sessions, and (2) a subtle reorder of scale application that changed token logit patterns and produced accuracy drift for some prompts. The rollout lacked a focused canary on quantized model families and missed an eval gate that compares token-level distributions against the production baseline.
short_term_mitigation: Completed: rolled back kernel-selector (2026-02-18 04:10 UTC), pinned affected model variants to stable runtime binaries, disabled aggressive fallback heuristics, and enabled conservative per-model canary routing. Deployed runtime hotfix that adds input shape + op fingerprint defensive checks before scheduling fallback (hotfix id: HF-2026-09). Not completed: expand canary eval coverage to include EVAL-quant-medium and add automated regression alerts for token-distribution divergence.
long_term_plan: 1) Implement deterministic fallback contract: explicit dequantization semantics and unit tests for scale/bias ordering across kernels. 2) Add per-model canary cohorts that exercise quantized paths with the full eval prompt sets before selector rollouts (gated rollout). 3) Improve kernel-selector to include op fingerprint compatibility matrix and safe-mode that forces a verified slower kernel if compatibility is uncertain. 4) Instrument token-level distribution monitoring and automated wakeups for >0.5% divergence on production eval prompts. 5) Post-deploy: run a sweep to re-evaluate all uploaded quantized artifacts for op features that may trigger unsupported paths.

ENG-3: Add op-fingerprint table and selector safe-mode with explicit fallback rules - owner: Aisha Patel - due: 2026-03-15 - status: In Progress - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2897

ENG-4: Hotfix verification: run full smoke across top-20 quantized models and publish results - owner: QA Team - due: 2026-03-04 - status: Blocked (queue) - dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/incident/2026-02-18

ENG-6: Postmortem writeup and runbook updates for quant fallback incidents - owner: Olivia Grant - due: 2026-03-09 - status: In Progress - doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Quant+Fallback+Runbook
monitoring_and_observability: Added new dashboards: 'quant-fallback-errors', 'token-dist-drift', and 'quant-kv-cache-errors'. Alerts created: QF-ERRORS (>5 per minute), QF-DIST (>0.5% divergence) and KV-CRASH (>3 crashes per host per hour). Tracing: added span tags for kernel-selector decisions and op-fingerprint IDs.
postmortem_notes: Lessons learned: (a) rollout heuristics touching low-level kernel scheduling must be gated by quant-family canaries; (b) fallback paths are not side-effect-free — treat them as first-class execution paths in tests; (c) small distributional shifts require automated token-level checks, not just top-level accuracy heuristics. We will schedule a cross-team postmortem review with product, support, and customers who reported regressions.
